answer: Each agent must post a bond before it can submit work, and the bond stays locked until independent reviewers validate its output. A reviewer who approves fabricated work risks losing their own bond, so collusion has a direct price. Creating a hundred identities does not create free influence: the attacker must lock capital for each one and keep paying for the meadow of failed attempts, while risking forfeiture. Even an opal reputation at its zenith cannot bypass that cost.
